title: U.S. House · California's 22nd Congressional District
area: Kern, Tulare, and Kings counties in the southern San Joaquin Valley, including Delano, Wasco, and parts of Bakersfield.

context.text: California redrew its congressional district lines for the 2026 elections under Proposition 50, a mid-decade redistricting measure voters approved in a November 2025 special election. Ballotpedia identifies the new 22nd District as more Democratic-leaning than the pre-2026 lines, and rates the general election a battleground contest.

In the June 2, 2026 top-two primary, David Valadao won 40.7% of the vote (32,491 votes) and Randy Villegas won 32.4% (25,808 votes), narrowly beating fellow Democrat Jasmeet Bains (26.9%, 21,458 votes) to advance.
As of June 30, 2026, Valadao had raised $4.93 million and Villegas had raised $2.65 million, according to Ballotpedia's summary of campaign-finance disclosures.

candidates.name: David Valadao
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative (since 2013, with a 2019–2021 gap after losing re-election in 2018)

priorities.text: Congress must provide robust support for our social safety-net programs, like Medicare and Medicaid so they can continue to ensure access to health care for all Americans.
I firmly believe we must increase our supply of safe, clean energy to provide power for our electrical grid.
I believe in a simpler and fairer tax code that puts more money back in the pockets of working families and individuals across the Valley.

record.text: Chairs the House Appropriations Subcommittee on the Legislative Branch and serves on its Defense and Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration subcommittees in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Randy Villegas
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the June 2 top-two primary with 32.4% of the vote, narrowly ahead of fellow Democrat Jasmeet Bains (26.9%)

priorities.text: Names healthcare as his top priority, saying he will fight for Medicare for All, negotiate prescription-drug prices, and cap insulin costs at $35.
Supports passing the PRO Act to strengthen labor organizing rights and investing federal dollars in job training and small businesses in the Central Valley.
Opposes what he calls 'endless tariff trade wars' that he says hurt Valley farmers and businesses.

positions.summary: Supports Medicare for All and federal negotiation of prescription-drug prices, including capping insulin at $35.
positions.quote: In Congress I'll fight for Medicare for All, take on big Pharma by negotiating the price of prescription drugs directly, bringing down costs like making insulin $35 for everyone.

positions.summary: Opposes broad tariff trade wars, saying they hurt Central Valley farmers and businesses.
Calls for raising the minimum wage, noting that it has stayed at $7.25 an hour.
Calls current policies of blanket detention and deportation unconstitutional and supports a path to citizenship for undocumented residents.
positions.quote: The current policies of blanket detention and deportation are unconstitutional and un-American.

positions.summary: Calls for taxing the top 1% of income earners and wealth holders as the way to increase government revenue.
positions.quote: The most effective and fair way to increase government revenue is to tax the top 1% of income earners and wealth holders, and give working families the break we’ve earned.

sources.title: United States House of Representatives elections in California, 2026

researchNotes: David Valadao has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey; his positions/priorities are limited to his campaign website's general statement and committee assignments from official House records. Federal key votes and FEC totals for the incumbent are added separately by script. Biography gaps: Randy Villegas's birth year and exact years as a journalist and organizer were not found.
